subject: Short-term concurrency cushion and reconciliation options for Shoply launch spike
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maggie Liu <maggie@shoply.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term concurrency cushion and reconciliation options for Shoply launch spike

Hi Maggie —

Congrats again on the upcoming launch. We reviewed the telemetry you shared and understand you expect a brief window of 8–12x normal concurrency for a ~48–72 hour period starting next Tuesday UTC. To avoid throttling during that window, we can provision a temporary concurrency cushion.

Option A (standard): +50% concurrency for 72 hours, charged at PAYG overrun rates (no discount). Invoices will show the overrun and we'll true-up on next monthly invoice.

Option B (concession): +40% concurrency for 72 hours with no immediate surcharge. Instead, overrun usage will be true-upped at PAYG but we apply a one-time settlement credit equal to 30% of the overrun charge if Shoply converts to a 6-month Dedicated trial within 30 days after the event.

Operational notes:
- We can activate the cushion with >=24 hours notice.
- We'll enable a transient routing policy to your preferred region (us-west) and set a conservative KV cache warming strategy to limit regen cost.
- If you'd like, we can enable a short-term soft-throttle at 95% of the cushion to provide advance warning via webhooks.

Attached: temp_quota_addendum.pdf (draft addendum).

Next steps: pick A or B, confirm the start window, and sign the addendum (DocuSign link included in the addendum). If you prefer, we can deploy the cushion in test on Tuesday morning and cutover to prod once you confirm traffic shape.

Best,
Sean
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

---
Attachment: temp_quota_addendum.pdf (pdf, 42KB): short addendum outlining temporary quota increase, activation terms, and billing reconciliation guidance.)

From: Maggie Liu <maggie@shoply.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Shoply Ops <ops@shoply.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 12:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term concurrency cushion and reconciliation options for Shoply launch spike

Thanks Sean — this is super helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) The spike window is currently expected to be ~36 hours concentrated during our promotional drop (Wed 02:00–38:00 UTC). We'll have a clearer number by Monday EOD once the marketing team finishes the traffic forecast.

2) Budget-wise we'd prefer Option B (concession) if the settlement credit is straightforward to document — legal prefers credits over surcharges for one-off launch support.

3) Can we cap the maximum overrun billable at 2x our PAYG baseline for the 72-hour period? If not, we'd like to understand the downside exposure so we can plan a contingency PO.

Attached our internal launch_schedule.xlsx with the forecasted peak windows and endpoints.

If Option B is workable, we'll route legal to the DocuSign you send and loop finance for PO prep.

—Maggie
Maggie Liu
Head of Platform, Shoply
maggie@shoply.com

Attachment: launch_schedule.xlsx (xlsx, 18KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Maggie Liu <maggie@shoply.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term concurrency cushion and reconciliation options for Shoply launch spike

Sean / Irene — quick internal note then I'll loop back with Maggie.

Proposed commercial concession (to make Option B cleaner for Shoply legal):
- Offer +40% concurrency for up to 72 hours with activation on notice.
- No immediate surcharge during that window. Any overrun measured will be invoiced at standard PAYG rates on the next cycle.
- Apply a one-time settlement credit equal to 30% of the measured overrun charge if Shoply signs a 6-month Dedicated trial (min commitment: $X/mo equivalent) within 30 days after the event.
- Cap: we should avoid open-ended caps on invoice liability — instead, offer a protective soft-cap language: if measured overrun > 200% of baseline for the window, apply an emergency review and pause further consumption until Shoply confirms acceptance of a temporary cap or PO. This gives us both protection and a predictable escalation path.

I put the formal wording in concession_terms.docx (outline for legal). We can offer Shoply a simple clause that sets the emergency review trigger and the credit mechanics.

If that sounds OK to you both, I'll send the DocuSign with the addendum language and a PR to billing to track the potential credit as a contingent liability.

Ben
Senior Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
---
Attachment: concession_terms.docx (docx, 12KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maggie Liu <maggie@shoply.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term concurrency cushion and reconciliation options for Shoply launch spike

Maggie — thanks for the quick reply and for the schedule. Option B is approved internally with the emergency review language Ben suggested (we updated the addendum to reflect the trigger at >200% of baseline). Summary of agreed path: 

- Activation: +40% concurrency cushion for 72 hours starting at the observed spike start (you can give us >=24h notice).
- Billing: No immediate surcharge during the window; usage beyond baseline will be invoiced at PAYG on next invoice.
- Credit: If Shoply signs a 6-month Dedicated trial within 30 days, Redwood will apply a one-time settlement credit equal to 30% of the billed overrun for the event.
- Emergency protection: if run rate exceeds 200% of baseline in the window, we will trigger an emergency review and temporarily halt additional consumption subject to Shoply's approval or an emergency PO — this prevents runaway billing while allowing normal spikes.

Next steps for Shoply:
1) Confirm acceptance of the above.
2) Sign the addendum via DocuSign here: https://docusign.com/abc123-temp-quota-addendum
3) If accepted, provide start-window notice >=24h before go-live.

I'll loop in Billing once you sign so the true-up and credit plumbing are prepped on our side. Happy to jump on a short call Monday if you want to walk through the math.

Cheers,
Sean
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198
